# Native decision images

Run from the repository root after obtaining the pinned llama.cpp checkout:

```sh
bash backend/cpp/llama-cpp/tests/verify-decision-images.sh
```

Prerequisites: C++17, zlib and libjpeg development headers/libraries, Python 3
with Pillow (fixture generation only). Ubuntu: `libjpeg-dev zlib1g-dev`;
macOS: `brew install jpeg-turbo zlib`. CMake requires these libraries only when
the checkout has native decisions; older forks retain their dependency guard.
Both Docker builder paths install the packages in the shared compile stage,
including builds using cached base images. Darwin CI installs the Homebrew
packages. The llama.cpp packager collects the executable dependency closure, including
zlib/libjpeg. Darwin uses its existing dylib collection.

This compiles the production validation helper with upstream stb, zlib and
libjpeg. zlib requires a complete stream and valid Adler-32 within a fixed
output budget. libjpeg decodes all scans with warnings treated as errors, so
synthetic EOI recovery and short entropy scans cannot pass. Dimensions and
aggregate pixels are checked before decoder pixel/coefficient allocation. It checks
strict base64, MIME matching, count/byte/dimension/pixel limits, PNG decompression
bombs, invalid Adler-32 with valid chunk CRC, baseline/progressive JPEG,
missing EOI, truncated scans with appended EOI, embedded markers, truncation, chat-only collection, Anthropic normalization, empty-image
text limits, capability combinations, and parity with Go's canonical limits.
Fixtures are generated locally; no image or model downloads occur.

Build the native backend normally with `make backends/llama-cpp`. For a prepared
CPU checkout and extracted distro gRPC dependencies, the existing adapter is:

```sh
DEPS_ROOT=/path/to/deps CPU_BUILD=/path/to/llama.cpp/build-cpu \
  bash backend/cpp/llama-cpp/tests/build-decision-bridge.sh
```

The adapter compiles the actual prepared grpc-server.cpp and links upstream CPU
libraries. It is not a replacement implementation or mocked backend.

Start the resulting `grpc-server --addr=127.0.0.1:50061`, then run:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=/path/to/build-decision-validation \
python3 backend/cpp/llama-cpp/tests/decision-image-smoke.py \
  --model /models/OpenJev-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --projector /models/mmproj-OpenJev-Q8_0.gguf \
  --fixtures backend/cpp/llama-cpp/llama.cpp/build-image-tests/fixtures.json
```

The smoke uses CPU only, four threads, one slot, 8192 context, batch 512. It first
loads without a projector and asserts explicit unsupported plus direct-RPC
safety errors, then loads with the projector and compares red/blue probabilities.
It requires existing weights and a checksum-verified projector; it downloads
nothing. These are direct RPC tests, **not** public HTTP/router E2E evidence.

Check the production CMake dependency block and the non-decision fork guard:

```sh
python3 backend/cpp/llama-cpp/tests/verify-image-build-wiring.py
```

This focused check does not replace a full backend or platform build.

## CI gate

`.github/workflows/decision-images.yml` runs both verification commands on
relevant pull requests and master pushes, or by manual dispatch. It installs
C++17, Python/Pillow, CMake, zlib and libjpeg development dependencies and fetches
only the two vendor headers at `LLAMA_VERSION` from the backend Makefile (not a
floating upstream branch). No model, projector, GPU or full backend build is
needed. The path filters include this workflow, the backend helper/tests/build
files and upstream pin, Go limits, Dockerfiles and Darwin dependency setup.

This gate is separate from `backend/cpp/run-unit-tests.sh`: that stdlib-only
runner discovers `*_test.cpp`, not the dependency-bearing `decision-images.cpp`.

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
package policy

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"path/filepath"
	"time"

	. "github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2"
	. "github.com/onsi/gomega"
)

var _ = Describe("fail-soft reconcile", func() {
	It("keeps a record whose existence cannot be established and settles the rest", func() {
		dir := filepath.Join(GinkgoT().TempDir(), "policy")
		f := open(ModeNamedUser, dir)
		owner := named("owner")
		ctx := context.Background()
		down, _ := f.policy.Register(ctx, owner, "tables")
		made, _ := f.policy.Register(ctx, owner, "fixture")
		gone, _ := f.policy.Register(ctx, owner, "fixture")
		kept, _ := f.policy.Register(ctx, owner, "fixture")
		Expect(f.policy.Commit(ctx, owner, kept)).To(Succeed())
		Expect(f.store.Close()).To(Succeed())
		g := open(ModeNamedUser, dir)
		exists := func(_ context.Context, k ResourceKey) (bool, error) {
			switch k.ResourceID {
			case down.ResourceID:
				return false, ErrUnavailable
			case made.ResourceID:
				return true, nil
			}
			return false, nil
		}
		rep, err := g.policy.ReconcileReport(ctx, exists)
		Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
		Expect(rep).To(Equal(ReconcileReport{Settled: 2, Kept: 1}))
		pend, _ := g.policy.Pending()
		Expect(pend).To(Equal([]string{down.ResourceID}))
		Expect(allowed(g, owner, made, ActionRead)).To(BeTrue())
		Expect(allowed(g, owner, kept, ActionRead)).To(BeTrue())
		Expect(allowed(g, owner, down, ActionRead)).To(BeFalse())
		Expect(allowed(g, owner, gone, ActionRead)).To(BeFalse())
		// A later pass with an answer settles the kept record.
		Expect(g.policy.Reconcile(ctx, func(context.Context, ResourceKey) (bool, error) { return true, nil })).To(Succeed())
		Expect(allowed(g, owner, down, ActionRead)).To(BeTrue())
	})

	It("never drops a committed resource and counts pending quota unchanged", func() {
		f := open(ModeNamedUser, filepath.Join(GinkgoT().TempDir(), "policy"))
		owner := named("owner")
		ctx := context.Background()
		c, _ := f.policy.Register(ctx, owner, "tables")
		Expect(f.policy.Commit(ctx, owner, c)).To(Succeed())
		_, _ = f.policy.Register(ctx, owner, "tables")
		before, _ := f.policy.Pending()
		for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
			Expect(f.policy.Reconcile(ctx, func(context.Context, ResourceKey) (bool, error) { return false, errors.New("down") })).To(Succeed())
		}
		after, _ := f.policy.Pending()
		Expect(after).To(Equal(before))
		Expect(allowed(f, owner, c, ActionRead)).To(BeTrue())
	})

	It("retries kept records from the loop on a tick and on a kick, and stops on Close", func() {
		f := open(ModeNamedUser, filepath.Join(GinkgoT().TempDir(), "policy"))
		owner := named("owner")
		ctx := context.Background()
		a, _ := f.policy.Register(ctx, owner, "tables")
		b, _ := f.policy.Register(ctx, owner, "tables")
		ready := false
		exists := func(context.Context, ResourceKey) (bool, error) {
			if !ready {
				return false, ErrUnavailable
			}
			return true, nil
		}
		ticks := make(chan time.Time)
		reports := make(chan ReconcileReport, 4)
		l := NewReconcileLoop(f.policy, exists, ticks)
		l.Report = func(r ReconcileReport, _ error) { reports <- r }
		l.Start(ctx)
		ticks <- time.Time{}
		Expect(<-reports).To(Equal(ReconcileReport{Kept: 2}))
		ready = true
		l.Kick()
		Expect(<-reports).To(Equal(ReconcileReport{Settled: 2}))
		Expect(allowed(f, owner, a, ActionRead)).To(BeTrue())
		Expect(allowed(f, owner, b, ActionRead)).To(BeTrue())
		// Nothing pending: a tick does no work and reports nothing.
		ticks <- time.Time{}
		l.Close()
		Expect(reports).To(BeEmpty())
		l.Close()
	})

	It("closes a loop that never started without waiting", func() {
		f := open(ModeNamedUser, filepath.Join(GinkgoT().TempDir(), "policy"))
		NewReconcileLoop(f.policy, nil, nil).Close()
	})
})

package ociimage

import (
	"context"
	"path/filepath"
	"time"

	. "github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2"
	. "github.com/onsi/gomega"
)

var _ = Describe("LockFile", func() {
	It("returns the context error while the lock is held", func() {
		p := filepath.Join(GinkgoT().TempDir(), "x.lock")
		unlock, err := LockFile(context.Background(), p)
		Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 200*time.Millisecond)
		defer cancel()
		_, err = LockFile(ctx, p)
		Expect(err).To(MatchError(context.DeadlineExceeded))
		unlock()
		again, err := LockFile(context.Background(), p)
		Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred(), "after the release")
		again()
	})
})

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""Run the image workflow's real publication gate with disposable git history."""

import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
import tempfile
import textwrap
import unittest


WORKFLOW = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "workflows" / "image.yml"


def gate_script():
    # This deliberately supports only the workflow's block-scalar layout, not
    # arbitrary YAML. Fail closed if the job/step becomes ambiguous or moves.
    lines = WORKFLOW.read_text().splitlines()
    jobs = [i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if re.fullmatch(r" +changes:", line)]
    if len(jobs) != 1:
        raise AssertionError("expected one changes job")
    start = jobs[0]
    indent = len(lines[start]) - len(lines[start].lstrip())
    end = next((i for i in range(start + 1, len(lines))
                if lines[i].strip() and not lines[i].lstrip().startswith("#")
                and len(lines[i]) - len(lines[i].lstrip()) <= indent), len(lines))
    job = lines[start + 1:end]
    steps = [i for i, line in enumerate(job)
             if re.fullmatch(r" +- id: decide", line)]
    if len(steps) != 1:
        raise AssertionError("expected one changes -> decide step")
    start = steps[0]
    indent = len(job[start]) - len(job[start].lstrip())
    end = next((i for i in range(start + 1, len(job))
                if job[i].strip() and not job[i].lstrip().startswith("#")
                and len(job[i]) - len(job[i].lstrip()) <= indent), len(job))
    step = job[start + 1:end]
    runs = [i for i, line in enumerate(step) if re.fullmatch(r" +run: \|", line)]
    if len(runs) != 1:
        raise AssertionError("expected one literal run block in changes -> decide")
    start = runs[0]
    indent = len(step[start]) - len(step[start].lstrip())
    end = next((i for i in range(start + 1, len(step))
                if step[i].strip()
                and len(step[i]) - len(step[i].lstrip()) <= indent), len(step))
    script = textwrap.dedent("\n".join(step[start + 1:end]))
    if not script.strip():
        raise AssertionError("empty changes -> decide run block")
    return script + "\n"


class ImagePublicationGate(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.script = gate_script()

    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="image-publication-gate-")
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.repo = Path(self.tmp.name) / "repo"
        self.repo.mkdir()
        self.git("init", "--quiet")
        self.git("config", "user.name", "Gate Test")
        self.git("config", "user.email", "gate-test@example.invalid")
        self.git("config", "commit.gpgsign", "false")
        self.git("commit", "--quiet", "--allow-empty", "-m", "base")
        self.before = self.git("rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
        self.after = self.before

    def git(self, *args):
        return subprocess.run(
            ["git", *args], cwd=self.repo, check=True, text=True,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, timeout=30,
        ).stdout

    def change(self, paths):
        for name in paths:
            path = self.repo / name
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path.write_text("fixture\n")
        self.git("add", ".")
        self.git("commit", "--quiet", "-m", "changes")
        self.after = self.git("rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()

    def assert_gate(self, expected, before=None, ref="refs/heads/master"):
        output = Path(self.tmp.name) / "output"
        output.write_text("")
        env = dict(os.environ, BEFORE=self.before if before is None else before,
                   AFTER=self.after, GITHUB_REF=ref, GITHUB_OUTPUT=str(output),
                   LC_ALL="C")
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", "-e", "-o", "pipefail", "-c", self.script],
            cwd=self.repo, env=env, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE, timeout=30,
        )
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(output.read_text(), f"build={str(expected).lower()}\n",
                         result.stdout[-250:] + result.stderr)

    def test_small_code(self):
        self.change(["core/main.go"])
        self.assert_gate(True)

    def test_small_mixed(self):
        self.change(["core/main.go", "docs/guide.txt", "README.md"])
        self.assert_gate(True)

    def test_excluded_classes(self):
        for path in ["docs/guide.txt", "gallery/model.yaml", "examples/demo.py",
                     "README.md", "core/nested/notes.md"]:
            with self.subTest(path=path):
                self.before = self.after
                self.change([path])
                self.assert_gate(False)

    def large_paths(self):
        paths = [f"docs/guide-{i:05d}-{'x' * 55}.txt" for i in range(3500)]
        self.assertGreater(len(paths), 2869)
        self.assertGreater(len(("\n".join(paths) + "\n").encode()), 140000)
        return paths

    def test_large_mixed_early_match_repeated(self):
        # Sorting puts the code match first, with far more than a pipe buffer
        # behind it. Repeat to guard against scheduling-dependent SIGPIPE.
        self.change(["aaa-code.go", *self.large_paths()])
        diff = self.git("diff", "--name-only", self.before, self.after)
        self.assertTrue(diff.startswith("aaa-code.go\n"))
        self.assertGreater(len(diff.encode()), 140000)
        self.assertGreater(len(diff.splitlines()), 2869)
        for attempt in range(8):
            with self.subTest(attempt=attempt):
                self.assert_gate(True)

    def test_large_excluded_only(self):
        self.change(self.large_paths())
        self.assert_gate(False)

    def test_empty_diff(self):
        self.assert_gate(True)

    def test_missing_zero_unresolvable_base(self):
        self.change(["docs/guide.txt"])
        for before in ["", "0" * 40, "f" * 40]:
            with self.subTest(before=before):
                self.assert_gate(True, before=before)

    def test_tag_push(self):
        self.change(["docs/guide.txt"])
        self.assert_gate(True, ref="refs/tags/v-test")
        self.assert_gate(True, before="", ref="refs/tags/v-test")
        self.assert_gate(True, before=self.after, ref="refs/tags/v-test")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

# MLX-Video on Apple Silicon

Install the backend and start LocalAI with the example model configuration:

```bash
local-ai backends install mlx-video
local-ai run --models-path ./examples/mlx-video
```

Generate a short video:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/video \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "ltx2-mlx",
    "prompt": "Ocean waves at golden hour, locked camera",
    "width": 768,
    "height": 512,
    "num_frames": 49,
    "fps": 24
  }'
```

MLX-Video and its models require substantial unified memory. Reduce the canvas
and frame count first if generation exhausts memory.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""Same-run fixture integrity and source freshness, without product builds."""
import importlib.util
import io
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile
import tempfile
import time
import unittest
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('fixtures', ROOT / 'scripts/ci/fixtures.py')
fixtures = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(fixtures)

class Fixtures(unittest.TestCase):
    def make(self, root):
        for name in ['core/http/react-ui/dist/index.html', 'pkg/grpc/proto/backend.pb.go',
                     'pkg/grpc/proto/backend_grpc.pb.go', 'pkg/motion/proto/motion.pb.go'] + fixtures.BINARIES:
            path = root / name
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path.write_text('fixture')
            if name in fixtures.BINARIES:
                path.chmod(0o755)

    def test_toolchain_identity_ignores_patch_releases(self):
        ident = fixtures.toolchain_identity
        self.assertEqual(ident('go', 'go version go1.26.9 linux/amd64'), ident('go', 'go version go1.26.10 linux/amd64'))
        self.assertNotEqual(ident('go', 'go version go1.26.9 linux/amd64'), ident('go', 'go version go1.27.0 linux/amd64'))
        self.assertEqual(ident('node', 'v22.12.0'), ident('node', 'v22.23.1'))
        self.assertNotEqual(ident('node', 'v22.12.0'), ident('node', 'v24.0.0'))
        self.assertNotEqual(ident('protoc', 'libprotoc 26.1'), ident('protoc', 'libprotoc 26.2'))

    def test_roundtrip_modes_paths_sha_and_checksums(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = Path(tmp); src = root/'src'; dst = root/'dst'
            src.mkdir(); dst.mkdir(); self.make(src)
            archive = root/'fixtures.tgz'
            fixtures.transfer('pack', src, archive, 'abc', {'go': '1.26'})
            fixtures.transfer('unpack', dst, archive, 'abc', {'go': '1.26'})
            self.assertEqual(fixtures.metadata(src), fixtures.metadata(dst))
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(AssertionError, 'sha mismatch'):
                fixtures.transfer('unpack', dst, archive, 'def', {'go': '1.26'})
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(AssertionError, 'tools mismatch'):
                fixtures.transfer('unpack', dst, archive, 'abc', {'go': '1.27'})
            manifest = src/'addon-fixtures.json'
            manifest.write_text(manifest.read_text().replace('production-v1', 'production-v2'))
            with tarfile.open(root/'config.tgz', 'w:gz') as tar:
                for name in fixtures.PATHS + ['addon-fixtures.json']:
                    tar.add(src/name, arcname=name)
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(AssertionError, 'config mismatch'):
                fixtures.transfer('unpack', dst, root/'config.tgz', 'abc', {'go': '1.26'})
            with tarfile.open(archive, 'w:gz') as tar:
                payload = b'escape'; member = tarfile.TarInfo('../escape'); member.size = len(payload)
                tar.addfile(member, io.BytesIO(payload))
            with self.assertRaises(AssertionError):
                fixtures.transfer('unpack', dst, archive, 'abc', {'go': '1.26'})

    def test_restore_rebases_freshness_only_after_identity_validation(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = Path(tmp); src = root/'src'; dst = root/'dst'
            src.mkdir(); dst.mkdir(); self.make(src)
            old = time.time_ns()-10_000_000_000
            for name in fixtures.metadata(src): os.utime(src/name, ns=(old, old))
            archive = root/'fixtures.tgz'; fixtures.transfer('pack', src, archive, 'abc')
            # A separate checkout occurs after the producer built its files.
            sources = ['core/http/react-ui/src/components/addons/RecoveryPanel.jsx',
                       'core/http/react-ui/src/components/addons/recoveryState.js',
                       'core/http/react-ui/src/utils/addonsApi.js',
                       'core/services/addons/recovery/backup.go',
                       'core/http/endpoints/addons/recovery.go', 'tests/e2e/mock-backend/main.go']
            for name in sources:
                target = dst/name; target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); target.write_text('source')
            fixtures.transfer('unpack', dst, archive, 'abc')
            # Execute the exact freshness assertions from recovery.sh 33-39.
            text = (ROOT/'scripts/addons/recovery.sh').read_text()
            start = text.index('[ "$root/tests/e2e-ui/ui-test-server" -nt "$ui/dist/index.html" ]')
            end = text.index('\n\n', start)
            guard = text[start:end]
            env = dict(os.environ, root=str(dst), ui=str(dst/'core/http/react-ui'))
            self.assertEqual(subprocess.run(['sh', '-c', guard], env=env, capture_output=True).returncode, 0)
            source = dst/sources[3]
            later = (dst/'tests/e2e-ui/ui-test-server').stat().st_mtime_ns+1_000_000
            source.write_text('new edit'); os.utime(source, ns=(later, later))
            self.assertNotEqual(subprocess.run(['sh', '-c', guard], env=env, capture_output=True).returncode, 0)
            # Failed identity checks must not mark a stale binary fresh.
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(AssertionError, 'sha mismatch'):
                fixtures.transfer('unpack', dst, archive, 'different')
            self.assertLess((dst/'tests/e2e-ui/ui-test-server').stat().st_mtime_ns, source.stat().st_mtime_ns)

    def test_missing_executable_and_tampered_payload(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = Path(tmp); self.make(root)
            binary = root/fixtures.BINARIES[0]; binary.chmod(0o644)
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(AssertionError, 'not executable'):
                fixtures.transfer('pack', root, root/'fixtures.tgz', 'abc')
            binary.chmod(0o755)
            fixtures.transfer('pack', root, root/'fixtures.tgz', 'abc')
            binary.write_text('tampered')
            # Pack files with the old manifest, emulating damaged artifact contents.
            with tarfile.open(root/'bad.tgz', 'w:gz') as tar:
                for name in fixtures.PATHS + ['addon-fixtures.json']:
                    tar.add(root/name, arcname=name)
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(AssertionError, 'checksum/mode mismatch'):
                fixtures.transfer('unpack', root, root/'bad.tgz', 'abc')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

# File text index (phase 1)

Tracking issue: https://github.com/mudler/LocalAI/issues/12990

## Problem

`search_files` and `GET /api/chats/files/search` read only UTF-8 text files
up to 1 MiB, and walk the tree on every call. A PDF, Word, Excel or
PowerPoint file is found by name only. A user who uploads a PDF with a
generated name cannot find it by a word inside it, even when the PDF has a
real text layer.

## Decisions

- Extract the text when a file is written (an upload, a chat tool, a sync,
  an undo), not when it is searched.
- Phase 1 types: PDF (text layer only), `.docx`, `.xlsx`/`.xlsm`, `.pptx`.
  No OCR, no audio, no model downloads.
- The text lives in LocalAI's own store, never as a file in the user's
  folders. One row per workspace node, keyed by node ID, with the content
  hash it was made from.
- In a cluster one frontend extracts (advisory lock), and every frontend
  searches the shared rows.

## Extraction

`core/services/studio/extract` stays the one entry: `Extract(ctx, name,
data)` for PDF and Office. PDF goes through the extractor it already uses
(PDFium in WebAssembly, no cgo). The add-ons' `pdfread` package is internal
to the add-ons and is not used. Changes:

- `Structure.Sections` lists where each page, sheet or slide starts in the
  text (a 1-based line), so a hit can say "page 3" or "sheet Budget".
- A PDF page starts with a `## Page N` line, as sheets and slides already
  start with `## Sheet` and `## Slide`. `read_document` gets the same text.
- `Limits.Pages` (default 200) stops a PDF after that many pages, and
  `Limits.Text` now also cuts a PDF. Both set `Truncated` and add a note.

## Store

Package `core/services/studio/textindex`. `Store` has two implementations
with one contract suite (`textindextest`):

- GORM (SQLite or PostgreSQL, the auth database): table
  `studio_file_texts`, one row per node: `node_id`, `path`, `owner`, `hash`,
  `extractor` (version), `status` (`pending`, `ready`, `failed`,
  `skipped`), `reason`, `kind`, `sections` (JSON), `text`, `folded` (the
  text in lower case, for matching), `truncated`, `bytes`, `updated`. A
  second table keeps the journal cursor.
  - SQLite: an FTS5 table with the trigram tokenizer over `folded`, kept in
    step by triggers, answers queries of three or more characters. If the
    driver has no FTS5, or the query is shorter, `instr(folded, ?)` is used.
  - PostgreSQL: a `pg_trgm` GIN index on `folded` when the extension can be
    created; the query is `folded LIKE '%q%'` either way.
- JSON (one process, no database): the metadata in one file, each text in
  its own file. Search reads the texts under the path one by one and
  matches them in memory. That is a scan, not an index, and it is
  acceptable for the single-process store.

The store answers candidates. The final match is always the Go matcher of
`search_files` run over the stored text line by line, so the semantics stay
the same: plain text is a case-insensitive substring, `regex: true` is RE2
per line. Regex search pages through the ready rows under the path.

## Access

A row is not a permission. At query time each candidate is checked with a
`Stat` of its path as the caller: the node must exist, be readable by the
caller, and have the same node ID and hash as the row. A file that the
caller cannot read, that moved, or that changed since it was indexed is not
shown. The text is never stored in a place that users read directly.

## Indexer

- The workspace journal is the queue. A pass reads `ChangesSince(admin,
  cursor)` in batches and applies each operation: a create or write of a
  supported file marks the row `pending` with the new hash (unchanged hash:
  only the path changes); a delete removes the row; a move changes the
  path, or the paths below a moved folder. The cursor is saved after each
  batch, so the pass resumes after a restart.
- The first pass starts at revision 0: replaying the journal is the
  backfill of existing files. It is rate limited by the batch budget of one
  pass and by the extraction concurrency.
- An upload (REST) and a write by a chat tool also mark the row `pending`
  at once and wake the indexer, so a search right after an upload says the
  file is being indexed instead of "nothing found".
- Extraction: at most 2 files at a time, 60 s each, a panic becomes
  `failed`, at most 50 MiB of input, text capped by
  `chats_index_max_text_bytes` (2 MiB by default) and 200 pages. A PDF with
  no text layer is `skipped` with reason `no text layer`. A hash that is
  ready on another row is copied, not extracted again.
- A purge (empty Trash, delete one entry for good) removes the rows of the
  nodes it erased, through a hook of the files service.
- Settings: `chats_index_files` (default on) and
  `chats_index_max_text_bytes`. Off: the indexer does no work and the
  search says nothing about pending files; rows that still match their file
  are used.

Distributed mode: single-runner. The pass runs under
`advisorylock.TryWithLockCtx` with a new key; the rows and the cursor are in
the shared database, so any frontend's search sees them. Without a database
(JSON store) the process is alone and runs the pass itself.

## Tools and REST

- `search_files`: name hits, then text-file lines (as before), then hits in
  indexed documents as `path (page 3, line 40): snippet`. When files under
  the path are still pending the answer ends with "2 files are still being
  indexed; search again in a moment." The description says it searches
  inside PDF, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files.
- `read_file` on a PDF or Office file returns the extracted text with the
  usual `offset`/`limit` (2000 lines). It uses the index when it matches the
  file, and extracts on the spot otherwise.
- `GET /api/chats/files/search`: hits gain `page`, `sheet` and `slide`, the
  result gains `indexing`. The Files page shows "page 3" instead of the line
  and a line that files are being indexed. No new route, so no new MCP tool:
  the route is the user's own files (see the existing skip in
  `api_instructions.go`).

## Tests

Store contract on JSON, SQLite and PostgreSQL (when
`LOCALAI_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` is set); extraction of synthetic fixtures built
in the test code; the indexer lifecycle (upload, overwrite, rename, folder
move, delete, purge, shared folder seen by two users, backfill, caps, panic,
two frontends on one database); the tools; a route test that uploads a
UUID-named PDF and finds it by a word inside with `search_files`.

## Not in phase 1

OCR, audio transcripts, model installs from a wizard, per-file status in the
Files page: see the issue.

# Face-recognition e2e fixtures

The face-recognition e2e tests (`tests/e2e-backends/backend_test.go`)
don't require committed fixture JPEGs. They follow the same pattern as
`BACKEND_TEST_AUDIO_URL` (whisper): the Makefile target passes
HTTP URLs via `BACKEND_TEST_FACE_IMAGE_*_URL`, and the suite downloads
them at `BeforeAll` time.

For the Makefile targets in `Makefile`, the defaults point at NASA's
public-domain astronaut portraits on nasa.gov. NASA images are released
into the public domain by U.S. federal work (see
<https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/>).

If you want to run the suite fully offline, drop three JPEGs into this
directory with the names the Makefile expects and flip the env vars to
the `_FILE` variants:

```
tests/fixtures/faces/person_a_1.jpg   # person A, photo 1
tests/fixtures/faces/person_a_2.jpg   # person A, photo 2 (different angle/lighting)
tests/fixtures/faces/person_b.jpg     # a different person
```

The suite asserts *relative* ordering only (`d(a1,a2) < d(a1,b)`) — the
absolute distance ceiling is set per-model via
`BACKEND_TEST_VERIFY_DISTANCE_CEILING` so SFace (which uses a wider
distance distribution than ArcFace) can share the same suite.

def load(projector):
    r = s.LoadModel(pb.ModelOptions(ModelFile=a.model, MMProj=projector,
        ContextSize=8192, NBatch=512, Threads=4, NGPULayers=0,
        Options=['parallel:1']), timeout=600)

        'criteria': {'red': None, 'blue': None}}}}

def score(b):

def reject(b, code):
    try:

"""Generate small compressed fixtures, including hostile IHDR/IDAT combinations."""
import base64
import json
import io
from PIL import Image
import struct
import sys
import zlib

def png(w, h, pixels):
    def chunk(kind, data):
        return struct.pack('>I', len(data)) + kind + data + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(kind + data))
    return b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + chunk(b'IHDR', struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) + chunk(b'IDAT', zlib.compress(pixels)) + chunk(b'IEND', b'')

def url(raw):
    return 'data:image/png;base64,' + base64.b64encode(raw).decode()

fixtures = {
    'aggregate': url(png(3000, 3000, (b'\0' * 9001)*3000)),
    'dimension': url(png(4097, 1, b'\0'*12292)),
    'pixels': url(png(4096, 4096, b'\0')),
    'bomb': url(png(1, 1, b'\0'*1000000)),
    'truncated': url(png(1, 1, b'\0'*4)[:-15]),
    'red': url(png(64, 64, (b'\0'+b'\xff\0\0'*64)*64)),
    'blue': url(png(64, 64, (b'\0'+b'\0\0\xff'*64)*64)),
}
bad = bytearray(png(1, 1, b'\0'*4))
bad[29] ^= 1
fixtures['bad_crc'] = url(bad)
# CRC-valid IDAT with an invalid zlib Adler-32 checksum.
bad = bytearray(base64.b64decode(fixtures['red'].split(',')[1]))
pos = bad.index(b'IDAT')
n = struct.unpack('>I', bad[pos-4:pos])[0]
bad[pos+4+n-1] ^= 1
bad[pos+4+n:pos+8+n] = struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(bad[pos:pos+4+n]))
try:
    zlib.decompress(bad[pos+4:pos+4+n])
    raise AssertionError('invalid Adler-32 accepted')
except zlib.error:
    pass
fixtures['bad_adler'] = url(bad)

def jpeg(w, h, progressive=False):
    out = io.BytesIO()
    Image.new('RGB', (w, h), 'red').save(out, format='JPEG', progressive=progressive)
    return out.getvalue()

def jpg_url(raw):
    return 'data:image/jpeg;base64,' + base64.b64encode(raw).decode()

jpg = jpeg(64, 64)
for key, raw in {
    'jpeg': jpg,
    'jpeg_progressive': jpeg(64, 64, True),
    # EOI inside a comment is data, not an end marker.
    'jpeg_embedded_marker': jpg[:2] + b'\xff\xfe\x00\x04\xff\xd9' + jpg[2:],
    'jpeg_missing_eoi': jpg[:-2],
    'jpeg_truncated_scan': jpg[:-30],
    'jpeg_appended_eoi': jpg[:-30] + b'\xff\xd9',
    'jpeg_embedded_missing_eoi': jpg[:2] + b'\xff\xfe\x00\x04\xff\xd9' + jpg[2:-2],
    'jpeg_dimension': jpeg(4097, 1),
    'jpeg_pixels': jpeg(4096, 4096),
}.items():
    fixtures[key] = jpg_url(raw)
json.dump(fixtures, open(sys.argv[1], 'w'))

# skills

`skills` finds the skills that apply to a chat and renders the index that goes
into the prompt. This package holds the mechanism. The chats service holds the data: it
decides which workspace folders are the roots of the layers, which skills a
chat switched off, and how the user sees them.

A skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` file. The frontmatter has a `name` and a
`description`. The body is a procedure that the agent loads by the skill's
name when a task matches. Other files in the folder (references, scripts) are
read by the agent with its normal file tools. The package never reads them.

```go
roots := []skills.Root{
	{Layer: skills.LayerBuiltin, Path: "/builtin-skills", Guest: "/workspace/shared-builtin-skills"},
	{Layer: skills.LayerShared, Path: "/skills", Guest: "/workspace/shared-skills"},
	{Layer: skills.LayerPersonal, Path: "/users/7/.skills", Guest: "/workspace/home/.skills"},
	{Layer: skills.LayerFolder, Path: "/users/7", Guest: "/workspace/home"},
}
list, notes, err := skills.Resolve(ctx, store, actor, roots, skills.Options{Off: chatSwitches})

// In the ChatTools hook of the session:
return session.TurnTools{
	Prompt:     skills.Index(list),
	Note:       strings.Join(notes, "; "),
	RefreshKey: hashOf(list), // changes when a SKILL.md is new or changed
}, nil
```

The sandbox of a chat sees only the files that existed when it was made.
`RefreshKey` tells `session` when to refresh it: a key that differs from the
key of the turn before refreshes the sandbox (its processes end). A switch
that only removes lines from the index needs no refresh, so it must not
change the key.

`session` does not import `skills`. The product joins them.

## Loading a skill

The index names no path. Its first line tells the model to call the product's
load tool (`LoadTool`, `load_skill`) with a skill's name. `Usable` returns the
skills that the index lists, in its order, so the tool and the index never
disagree: the product resolves once, `Find` picks the skill of a name and
`Body` returns the text of its `SKILL.md` after the frontmatter. For a name
that `Find` does not match, `Suggest` returns up to three near names: the same
name in other case, the name with a `<prefix>-` or `<layer>:` part added or
taken away, or a name one or two edits away. `Names` lists every usable name
for the error.

## Layers

| Layer | Root `Path` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `LayerBuiltin` | the layer folder | skills that ship with the product |
| `LayerAddon` | the folder of one add-on | skills an add-on ships; one root per add-on, with `Addon` and `AddonTitle` set |
| `LayerShared` | the layer folder | skills an administrator gives to everyone |
| `LayerPersonal` | the layer folder | the skills of one user |
| `LayerFolder` | a folder to walk | every `.skills` folder below it |

Each layer folder holds one subfolder per skill. For `LayerFolder`, `Resolve`
walks the folder breadth first, at most 6 levels deep and at most 2,000
folders per call, and uses each `.skills` folder it finds. It does not enter a
`.skills` folder, a layer folder that has its own root, or a path in
`Root.Skip` (a product skips a folder that holds many chat uploads, so that it
does not use the budget; a `.skills` folder inside it is not found).
`Options.Logger` gets the number of folders listed, at debug level. A walk that a limit
cuts adds the note `some folders were not searched for skills`.

`Resolve` reads through the actor. A folder that the actor cannot read gives
no skill and no error. It returns an error only when the store fails.

## Precedence

The nearest layer wins: folder, personal, shared, built-in. Between two folder
skills the deeper folder wins; at equal depth the path that sorts first wins.
A skill that loses to one with the same name has `Shadowed` set to the layer
of the winner and is not in the index. `Options.Off` runs before this rule, so
if it turns off only a nearer skill, the one below it is uncovered. The chats
turn off the winner for a plain name and one layer for `layer:name`
(skillsvc.go). A skill that was
switched off has `Off` set.

## Limits

| Item | Limit |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md` size | 64 KiB (`MaxFileSize`) |
| `name` | `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$` |
| `description` | not empty, at most 1,024 bytes after `Clean` (`MaxDescription`) |
| files read per `Resolve` | 200, nearest layers first; the note is `some skills were not read` |
| index | 100 skills and 16 KiB; a last line says `N more skills not listed` |

`Clean` removes control characters and invisible format characters (Unicode
category Cf, bidi overrides included) and folds runs of white space to one
space. A skill that breaks a limit is returned with `Invalid` set to the
reason. It is not in the index.

## Frontmatter

`Parse` reads a small subset of YAML: `key: value` lines, single or double
quoted values, and block scalars (`|`, `>`) for any key. Unknown keys, such as
`allowed-tools` or `license`, are ignored.

## Safety

A skill is text that the model follows. A document that the agent reads can try
to make it write a harmful skill. The package gives the product what it needs
to show the risk (`Hash`, `Layer`, `Path`); marking new and changed skills,
and undo of the turn that wrote one, are the product's job.

# LocalAI website

LocalAI documentation website

## Requirement
In this project, the Docsy theme component is pulled in as a Hugo module, together with other module dependencies:

```bash
$ hugo mod graph
hugo: collected modules in 566 ms
hugo: collected modules in 578 ms
github.com/google/docsy-example github.com/google/docsy@v0.5.1-0.20221017155306-99eacb09ffb0
github.com/google/docsy-example github.com/google/docsy/dependencies@v0.5.1-0.20221014161617-be5da07ecff1
github.com/google/docsy/dependencies@v0.5.1-0.20221014161617-be5da07ecff1 github.com/twbs/bootstrap@v4.6.2+incompatible
github.com/google/docsy/dependencies@v0.5.1-0.20221014161617-be5da07ecff1 github.com/FortAwesome/Font-Awesome@v0.0.0-20220831210243-d3a7818c253f
```

If you want to do SCSS edits and want to publish these, you need to install `PostCSS`

```bash
npm install
```

## Running the website locally

Building and running the site locally requires a recent `extended` version of [Hugo](https://gohugo.io).
You can find out more about how to install Hugo for your environment in our
[Getting started](https://www.docsy.dev/docs/getting-started/#prerequisites-and-installation) guide.

From the LocalAI repository root, run:

```bash
make docs
```

The Hugo configuration lives in the `docs` directory. To invoke Hugo
directly instead, run:

```bash
cd docs
hugo server
```

## Running a container locally

You can run docsy-example inside a [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/)
container, the container runs with a volume bound to the `docsy-example`
folder. This approach doesn't require you to install any dependencies other
than [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop) on
Windows and Mac, and [Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/install/)
on Linux.

1. Build the docker image 

   ```bash
   docker-compose build
   ```

1. Run the built image

   ```bash
   docker-compose up
   ```

   > NOTE: You can run both commands at once with `docker-compose up --build`.

1. Verify that the service is working. 

   Open your web browser and type `http://localhost:1313` in your navigation bar,
   This opens a local instance of the docsy-example homepage. You can now make
   changes to the docsy example and those changes will immediately show up in your
   browser after you save.

### Cleanup

To stop Docker Compose, on your terminal window, press **Ctrl + C**. 

To remove the produced images run:

```console
docker-compose rm
```
For more information see the [Docker Compose
documentation](https://docs.docker.com/compose/gettingstarted/).

## Troubleshooting

As you run the website locally, you may run into the following error:

```
➜ hugo server

INFO 2021/01/21 21:07:55 Using config file: 
Building sites … INFO 2021/01/21 21:07:55 syncing static files to /
Built in 288 ms
Error: Error building site: TOCSS: failed to transform "scss/main.scss" (text/x-scss): resource "scss/scss/main.scss_9fadf33d895a46083cdd64396b57ef68" not found in file cache
```

This error occurs if you have not installed the extended version of Hugo.
See this [section](https://www.docsy.dev/docs/get-started/docsy-as-module/installation-prerequisites/#install-hugo) of the user guide for instructions on how to install Hugo.

Or you may encounter the following error:

```
➜ hugo server

Error: failed to download modules: binary with name "go" not found
```

This error occurs if you have not installed the `go` programming language on your system.
See this [section](https://www.docsy.dev/docs/get-started/docsy-as-module/installation-prerequisites/#install-go-language) of the user guide for instructions on how to install `go`.
